54F, EW EMER. admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to HOSPICE
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Bacteremia; Malignant ascites; Retention of urine, unspecified
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum; Obstruction of bile duct; Malignant neoplasm of intrahepatic bile ducts; Other ureteric obstruction; Cholangitis; Mechanical complication due to other implant and internal device, not elsewhere classified; Escherichia coli [E. coli] infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site; Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled; Other and unspecified hyperlipidemia; Other sequelae of chronic liver disease; Anemia, unspecified
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: none
PROCEDURES: Replacement of stent (tube) in biliary or pancreatic duct; Other cholangiogram; Percutaneous abdominal drainage
MEDICATIONS: D5 1/2NS 1000mL IV; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3mL IV; NS (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV; Meropenem 500mg IV; Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 200mL IV; Vancomycin 1000mg IV; 1/2 NS 1000mL IV; 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000mL IV; *NF* Ertapenem Sodium 1g IV; Lorazepam 0.5mg PO; Lidocaine 1% 3.2mL SC; Ondansetron 8mg IV; Pantoprazole 40mg PO; Heparin 5000UNIT SC; NS 100mL IV; MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) 500mg IV; Cholestyramine 4gm PO; Docusate Sodium 100mg PO; Morphine Sulfate (Oral Soln.) 5-10mg PO; Insulin 0UNIT SC; Senna 2TAB PO; Ertapenem 1gm IM; Sucralfate 1gm PO
MICROBIOLOGY: URINE: ENTEROCOCCUS SP. [AMPICILLIN=S, NITROFURANTOIN=S, TETRACYCLINE=R, VANCOMYCIN=S] | URINE: STAPHYLOCOCCUS SPECIES | BLOOD CULTURE: ESCHERICHIA COLI [AMPICILLIN=R, CEFAZOLIN=R, TRIMETHOPRIM/SULFA=R, GENTAMICIN=R, TOBRAMYCIN=R, AMIKACIN=S, CEFTAZIDIME=R, CEFTRIAXONE=R, CIPROFLOXACIN=R, PIPERACILLIN=R, AMPICILLIN/SULBACTAM=R, CEFUROXIME=R, PIPERACILLIN/TAZO=S, CEFEPIME=R, MEROPENEM=S]
SERVICES: OMED
WARDS: Medicine; Hematology/Oncology; Emergency Department
_patient.note:
[1] The patient presented with bacteremia, malignant ascites, and retention of urine, unspecified.
[2] The primary diagnosis was secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum.
[3] Active diagnoses included secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum, obstruction of bile duct, malignant neoplasm of intrahepatic bile ducts, other ureteric obstruction, cholangitis, mechanical complication due to other implant and internal device, not elsewhere classified, Escherichia coli [E. coli] infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled, other and unspecified hyperlipidemia, other sequelae of chronic liver disease, and anemia, unspecified.
[4] Past medical history was none.
[5] Procedures performed included replacement of stent (tube) in biliary or pancreatic duct, other cholangiogram, and percutaneous abdominal drainage.
[6] Medications administered included D5 1/2NS 1000mL IV, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3mL IV, NS (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV, Meropenem 500mg IV, Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 200mL IV, Vancomycin 1000mg IV, 1/2 NS 1000mL IV, 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000mL IV, *NF* Ertapenem Sodium 1g IV, Lorazepam 0.5mg PO, Lidocaine 1% 3.2mL SC, Ondansetron 8mg IV, Pantoprazole 40mg PO, Heparin 5000UNIT SC, NS 100mL IV, MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) 500mg IV, Cholestyramine 4gm PO, Docusate Sodium 100mg PO, Morphine Sulfate (Oral Soln.) 5-10mg PO, Insulin 0UNIT SC, Senna 2TAB PO, Ertapenem 1gm IM, and Sucralfate 1gm PO.
[7] Urine culture grew Enterococcus sp. [AMPICILLIN=S, NITROFURANTOIN=S, TETRACYCLINE=R, VANCOMYCIN=S].
[8] Urine culture grew Staphylococcus species.
[9] Blood culture grew Escherichia coli [AMPICILLIN=R, CEFAZOLIN=R, TRIMETHOPRIM/SULFA=R, GENTAMICIN=R, TOBRAMYCIN=R, AMIKACIN=S, CEFTAZIDIME=R, CEFTRIAXONE=R, CIPROFLOXACIN=R, PIPERACILLIN=R, AMPICILLIN/SULBACTAM=R, CEFUROXIME=R, PIPERACILLIN/TAZO=S, CEFEPIME=R, MEROPENEM=S].
[10] The patient was managed by the OMED service.
[11] The patient was admitted to the Medicine ward.
[12] The patient was also evaluated by Hematology/Oncology and Emergency Department.
[13] The patient was discharged alive to HOSPICE.
